name: XP-Pen drawing tablets and pen displays
summary: XP-Pen pen tablets and pen displays. Without a driver the pen moves the pointer like a mouse, but pressure and the shortcut buttons do nothing.

linux.notes: Many XP-Pen tablets work with Linux's built-in uclogic driver. For full pressure and button support on any Linux distribution, OpenTabletDriver (free, open source) supports most XP-Pen models. XP-Pen also publishes Linux drivers on its website.

darwin.notes: Install XP-Pen's driver from the Download section of xp-pen.com, or the free and open-source OpenTabletDriver, then allow it in System Settings > Privacy & Security under Accessibility. No security changes are needed.

steps.title: Download OpenTabletDriver
steps.explain: A free, open-source tablet driver that supports most XP-Pen models. XP-Pen's own driver (Download section of xp-pen.com) works too.

steps.title: Allow the driver and replug the tablet
steps.explain: When macOS asks, allow the driver in System Settings > Privacy & Security. Then unplug the tablet, plug it back in and press "Check again".
